brief:
The incoming Trump administration and various advocacy groups are competing to define President Joe Biden's record on Gaza ahead of his departure from office, according to the Quincy Institute. Supporters of Biden's approach argue his administration provided humanitarian aid and pursued diplomatic efforts, while critics contend it failed to sufficiently pressure Israel to end the war.

The debate reflects deeper divisions within Democratic circles over U.S. policy in Gaza, with some voices calling for tougher stances and others defending the administration's balancing act between support for Israel and calls for civilian protection. How Biden's Gaza record is ultimately framed could influence Democratic strategy and international relations under the new administration.
title: Advocates scramble to reshape Biden's Gaza legacy before term ends
